- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often over-optimistically forecasts continuation; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- If model forecast is consistently below recent 5-day average, consider mean reversion bias — increase forecast toward historical mean or 10-day moving average.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) and price is falling, model often under-anticipates further decline; add 1–2% downward bias to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period volatility — especially after sentiment shifts to positive; add 1–3% upward adjustment for final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings, model tends to lag in capturing momentum — forecast should be adjusted to align with sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead.
